messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT AUTO-PAGE: elevated 5xx spike and tail latency increase across eu-central region starting ~1958456600. Alert: 5xx rate +42% over baseline, request drop to providers a/b. Paging #incidents and @oncall.
Alex W: oncall here — seeing the alert. taking lead. quick ask: are we seeing backend errors or infra OOMs? any customer-facing 503s reported?
Sara G: looks like a mix — stack shows backend 502s originating at inference gateway (kv cache misses up, cold starts spiking). also heavy tails from a single high-throughput tenant in eu-central-prod.
Mike Ops: I'm seeing provider A (eu-provider-1) reporting high GPU queue depth and rising preemption. provider B still fine. might be provider-side capacity pressure.
Lisa SRE: runbook suggests either partial drain + reroute or rapid brownout of nonessential features. recommend: 1) immediately limit per-tenant concurrency for top 5 noisy tenants; 2) initiate 30% regional drain to eu-west fallback; 3) enable small-model fallback for chat endpoints.
Paul CS: flagging customer impact: 2 paying enterprise tenants reported degraded latency. they're on older SLAs — need comms if we do any failover. I'll draft a short note if we know ETA.
Alex W: OK. Sara, can you throttle the noisy tenant(s) first? Mike, prepare provider reroute plan. Lisa, I'll coordinate the drain. Paul, hold off comms until we know the impact surface.
Sara G: starting per-tenant limits now. I will drop concurrent request cap from 100 -> 20 for tenant IDs: cust-phi, cust-neo, cust-boreal. command:

```
# temporary per-tenant throttle
redwoodctl quotas update --tenant cust-phi --concurrency 20 --scope eu-central
redwoodctl quotas update --tenant cust-neo --concurrency 20 --scope eu-central
redwoodctl quotas update --tenant cust-boreal --concurrency 20 --scope eu-central
```

Sara G: applied. metrics should reflect within 30-45s.
Mike Ops: prepping reroute. plan: shift 25% of new sessions to eu-west-2 and 10% to global-fallback until pressure subsides. will update routing policy in traffic manager. command preview:

```
# staged reroute
redwoodctl traffic patch --region eu-central --shift 25 --to eu-west-2 --policy staged
redwoodctl traffic patch --region eu-central --shift 10 --to global-fallback --policy staged
```

Mike Ops: will apply in 2m if no objections.
Lisa SRE: before we reroute, we should start a graceful drain on a subset of nodes to free up headroom and avoid a hard cutover. executing drain on 30% of host-pool-eu-central (canary groups 1 and 2). command:

```
# graceful drain canary
redwoodctl nodes drain --pool host-pool-eu-central --canary 1 --percent 15
redwoodctl nodes drain --pool host-pool-eu-central --canary 2 --percent 15
```

Lisa SRE: also enabling small-model fallback for chat endpoints to reduce token compute cost (no change to behavior for most customers, some slight latency changes). apply config:

```
# model fallback toggle
redwoodctl featureflip enable --name small-model-fallback --scope eu-central
```

Alex W: go ahead with throttles and drain. Mike do staged reroute after Lisa's drain starts. Paul, can you confirm affected customers list and contact priority?
Paul CS: confirmed list. cust-phi and cust-neo are priority P1s — I'm opening urgent incident emails now. drafting: "experiencing increased errors and latency in eu-central; we're performing traffic shaping and partial failover to mitigate." Will update with ETA.
product-bot: NOTE: enabling small-model-fallback may slightly change output distribution for some prompts. recommend enabling evaluation guard rails for top 3 prompt sets.
Sara G: throttle metrics showing drop in sustained RPS for those tenants. 5xx rate for eu-central core dropped from +42% to +18% within 1m.
Mike Ops: initiating staged reroute now (25% -> eu-west-2, 10% -> global-fallback). patch applied.

```
INFO applying traffic patch: shift 25% -> eu-west-2, 10% -> global-fallback
INFO staged policy: start
```

Lisa SRE: canaries draining — nodes in canary1 showing connection drain and KV cache migration logs. no OOMs seen in logs so far. snippets:

```
[drain] node-ef12: migrating 2200 KV entries
[drain] node-ef12: connections draining, active 12
```

Alex W: monitoring dashboard: error rate trending down, latency back to baseline for most endpoints, but tail p99 still elevated by ~15%. need to watch for rebound.
Mike Ops: reroute telemetry shows eu-west-2 absorbing most traffic, provider A queue depth decreasing.
Lisa SRE: enabling short-term quota changes cluster-wide to buy time: reduce default concurrency from 200 -> 120 in eu-central. applied.

```
redwoodctl cluster-config set --region eu-central --default-concurrency 120
```

Paul CS: sent first customer note to P1s with current mitigations and expected updates every 30m.
Sara G: 5xx now at +6% vs baseline. p99 still high but improving. nice work.
Alex W: keep the staged reroute for 20 minutes, then reassess. If stable, plan to drain an additional 10% and slow roll back throttles.
product-bot: Remind: record all config changes in the incident changelog. link: https://console.redwood/incident/1958456789/changelog
Sara G: logging changes now. list of steps done:
- per-tenant concurrency limits applied (cust-phi/neo/boreal)
- cluster default concurrency reduced
- small-model-fallback enabled
- canary drains started
- staged reroute applied

Lisa SRE: ops check: no customer-facing 5xx for non-throttled tenants. edge cache hit improved after KV migration.
Mike Ops: provider A shows lower preemption events. good sign.
Paul CS: customer replies: "thanks for quick action, saw improvements on our side" from cust-neo.
Alex W: plan for next 60m: keep mitigations in place, watch p50/p95/p99, prepare rollback plan for staged reroute if eu-central stabilizes. assign postmortem owner and timeline.
Alex W: assigning postmortem to Lisa SRE. deliverable: RCA and action items within 48h. I'll update SEV status in PagerDuty.
Lisa SRE: acknowledged. creating incident ticket and will collect logs and config diffs.
Alex W: ok team — monitoring looks stable. leaving this thread open for 1h. handoff to night oncall at 1958457000.
Sara G: handing off to @oncall in 10m. leaving runbook notes.
Paul CS: will continue customer comms. will escalate if any regressions.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied; severity degraded to SEV3. next automated check in 10m.
Alex W: thanks all. good coordination.
